# Le040 — `\Q\` numeric-character-reference at the upper Unicode boundary (U+10FFFF)

<!-- Auto-generated; edit `STEP_PROBLEM_CATALOG.md` instead. -->

**Section**: §12.1a (`12-1a-encoding`)  
**Fixture**: [`step-examples/12-1a-encoding/Le040.stp`](../../step-examples/12-1a-encoding/Le040.stp)  

## Sources
- 16-iso-spec ISO 10303-21 Ed.3 §6.4.3 (`\Q\xxxx\Q\` numeric-char ref)

## Description

Edition-3 `\Q\xxxx\Q\` encodes a character by its decimal Unicode scalar value between bracketing `\Q\` pairs. Many implementations either ignore `\Q\` entirely (passing digits through verbatim) or accept only values up to `0xFFFF` (BMP only). The largest legal Unicode scalar is `0x10FFFF` (decimal `1114111`); a kernel claiming Edition-3 conformance should be able to decode this upper boundary into a four-byte UTF-8 sequence.

## Reproducer recipe

`PRODUCT.name='top=\Q\1114111\Q\'` — the `\Q\..\Q\` payload is the decimal value of U+10FFFF.

## Expected kernel behavior

decode `\Q\NNN\Q\` payloads into the corresponding Unicode scalar; reject only values outside the legal scalar range (`> 0x10FFFF` or surrogate halves); do not silently truncate to BMP.

**Structured outcomes** (extracted from prose; for downstream auto-grading):
- allowed: `reject`
- disallowed: `silent-accept`

## Notes

**See also**: Le030, Le041, Le042. Validation observed: ifcopenshell terminates via process signal — the `\Q\..\Q\` form may interact badly with the parser's ASCII-only string decoder. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts the file and either truncates to BMP or passes the digits through verbatim; kernel mishandling — the catalog above forbids silent BMP truncation.
